updates.section: Phase 1 delivered (reverses_request_id column, model field, repository plumbing)
updates.content:
This phase delivered recommended Phase 1 of GP-008 only: the `reverses_request_id` column, the `LeaveRequest.reversesRequestId` field, and the repository plumbing. The `LeaveService.cancel` reversal branch (Phase 2), the wire/web read-model exposure (Phase 3) and the reversal tests (Phase 4) are NOT implemented — `cancelRequest` still mutates an APPROVED request in place.

- `migrations/20260914000000_add_reverses_request_id_to_leave_requests.js` (new) — knex alter-table migration adding a nullable `text` column `reverses_request_id` to `leave_requests`, with a self-referencing FK to `leave_requests.id` (`leave_requests_reverses_request_id_foreign`, default NO ACTION) and a UNIQUE index (`leave_requests_reverses_request_id_unique`). `exports.down` drops the unique index, then the FK, then the column. The header comment records the binding aggregation rule (below). The timestamp sorts after the existing `20260913000001` migration.
- `src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts` — `LeaveRequest` gained `reversesRequestId: string | null` appended LAST, after `cancelledAt`; the other 14 fields are unchanged in name, type and order. `CreateLeaveRequestInput` remains `Omit<LeaveRequest, 'id'>`, so it now requires `reversesRequestId`.
- `src/modules/leave/leave.repository.ts` — `reverses_request_id` carried end-to-end: added to the `LeaveRequestRow` interface, the `COLUMNS` SELECT list, `mapRow`, and the INSERT column/value lists (now 15 values). `ILeaveRepository` declares and `PgLeaveRequestRepository` implements `findByReversesRequestId(reversesRequestId: string, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveRequest | null>` — a plain `SELECT ... WHERE reverses_request_id = $1` returning `null` when absent, never throwing; it follows the existing optional-trailing-`PoolClient` / `db(client)` convention and opens no transaction. The column is deliberately absent from `FIELD_COLUMNS`/`UpdateLeaveRequestDto`, so `update` cannot write it (set at INSERT time only).
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — GP-008 open question 4 (aggregation double-counting) was promoted from an open question to a **[RESOLVED — BINDING RULE]**: any aggregation that sums `requestedDays` MUST filter on `reverses_request_id IS NULL`, because a reversal row copies the original's `requestedDays` verbatim (never re-derived, never zeroed).

**Divergences from the plan worth noting:**
- The phase spec constrained the change to three files (migration, model, repository) and stated no service or test file would be touched. Two further files changed, both forced by the model change: `src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts` (the `create` input literal in the request-creation path gained `reversesRequestId: null`, since `CreateLeaveRequestInput` now requires the field) and `tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts` (`FakeLeaveRepository` gained `findByReversesRequestId` to satisfy the extended `ILeaveRepository`, and the two `LeaveRequest` fixtures gained `reversesRequestId: null`). No route, controller, `index.ts`, shared-types or web file changed.
- The UNIQUE index is a plain UNIQUE on the nullable column, not a partial index (`WHERE reverses_request_id IS NOT NULL`); PostgreSQL permits many NULLs under a plain UNIQUE, so the two are functionally equivalent.
- The FK declares no `ON DELETE` behaviour, so it uses the default NO ACTION, matching the schema's other self-referencing FKs.

### LeaveRequest

| Field | Type | Required |
|-------|------|----------|
| id | string | true |
| employeeId | string | true |
| leaveTypeId | string | true |
| startDate | Date | true |
| endDate | Date | true |
| reason | string \| undefined | false |
| status | LeaveRequestStatus | true |
| approvedBy | string \| null | false |
| approvedAt | Date \| null | false |
| createdAt | Date | true |
| updatedAt | Date | true |
| reversesRequestId | string \| null | true |

**Relationships**
- `Employee` — many-to-one

**Reversal provenance (GP-008)** — `reversesRequestId` is `null` for every ordinary request and non-null only on a reversal row, where it equals the id of the original APPROVED request it reverses. It is set at INSERT time only and is never updated. A reversal row is born CANCELLED and is terminal/inert; at most one reversal row may exist per original request (UNIQUE index on `reverses_request_id`). Because a reversal row copies the original's `requestedDays` verbatim, any aggregation summing `requestedDays` MUST filter on `reverses_request_id IS NULL` or it double-counts.
